pr_title: If rendering has failed due to a net.OpError stop rendering
pr_body:
When a net.OpError occurs during rendering the underlying connection is essentially
dead and therefore attempting to render further data will only cause further errors.

Therefore in serverErrorInternal detect if the passed in error is an OpError and
if so do not attempt any further rendering.

Fix #18629

Signed-off-by: Andrew Thornton <art27@cantab.net>

Well this is irritating. 

```go
package main

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"net"
)

func main() {
	opError := &net.OpError{Op: "write", Net: "", Err: fmt.Errorf("random")}
	fmt.Println(opError)

	fmt.Println(errors.Is(opError, &net.OpError{}))
}
```

a `*net.OpError` does not pass `errors.Is(err, &net.OpError)`. 

We'll have to try again with just plain type checking because go's errors.Is just doesn't do what it should do.

review_comments:
```suggestion
		if errors.Is(logErr, net.OpError) {
```
shouldn't work this too ?

That won't compile. 

`net.OpError` is a `type` not an `error`, (`net.OpError` doesn't implement `error` either, `*net.OpError` would be the type that implements the `error` interface but is again a `type` not an `error`.)
For what's worth: go internally also use this error as a pointer: https://github.com/golang/go/blob/2ebe77a2fda1ee9ff6fd9a3e08933ad1ebaea039/src/internal/poll/error_test.go#L38 Approving.
